evidence: What holds. (a) Defining behaviour is graded heavily: hro_moves (w7), hro_bulk (w5), hro_undo_activity (w7), hro_interview_places (w5.5), hro_two_people (w4), hro_messaging (w6), hro_long_thread (w5.5) in tests/scored/functional/judge.toml lines 34-113. (b) Server-backed, not same-origin: gates/constraints/judge.toml hro_gate_shared (lines 45-52) requires a UI add, reload, and an Observer read in a new independent empty context, rejecting 'a static seed response, a no-op success message or a browser-only save'; every scored prompt repeats this check (functional/prompt.md line 15); hro_moves/hro_bulk/hro_undo_activity re-read orders as Mei Lin in an independent context. No criterion demands same-origin. (c) Reload/re-auth: hro_messaging step (3) keeps drafts through switch/Board/reload; polish hro_pol_session_resume (polish/judge.toml lines 56-62) ends the session mid-draft, requires the sign-in prompt, same-person resume and send, and that Mei on the same browser sees neither reply nor note draft. (d) Restart: hro_intake_restart (functional/judge.toml lines 25-32) calls restart_app once, signs in fresh, re-reads several records (both new jobs, J1 card order, a note, a message, unread total, J1 Activity lines, seeded Platform Engineer order and note) and checks no reseed; restart_app is declared only in functional (lines 14-18). Golden evidence: raw-evidence-index workspace.json (hash verified) records 'restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages, unread counts and activity without reseeding; live updates resume' passed=true on the frozen bytes; db.js seedIfEmpty never reseeds. DEFECT (lesson 15 pattern, 'Build several revisions, note each one's exact content, really restart, and re-read every one'). Every record hro_intake_restart reads after restart_app is created once and never revised: J1's six cards are only added (all still in Applied in insertion order), the note and message are inserts, and J1's Activity is only the opening plus additions. No card on J1 is moved, re-ordered, rejected or reopened before the restart, and no other criterion uses restart_app (it is single-use). So the board's defining mutable state (stage after a move, hand-arranged order within a stage, rejection reason and rejected-from stage) is never proven to survive a restart, although the public rules say so explicitly: hireops_rules.md lines 57-60 'We can move a card up or down within its stage ... and the order is still there after a reload, a fresh sign-in or a restart', and instruction.md line 17 'keep new work across restarts'. Secondary (shared with rows 26/28, lesson 16): hro_intake_restart is one binary (w4.5) that also grades job-opening validation (blank title, places 0/51/2.5, Recruiter-as-manager replay) and add-candidate validation (invalid/case-duplicate email, field-level message, form retention); a failure of any intake leg zeros the restart durability credit, so durability is not credited independently as REVIEW_POLICY 'Independent credit takes precedence over flow grouping' asks. Not a measurement waiver: no configured judge run, Oracle or model score exists for this candidate (raw-evidence-index scope says so).
counterexample: Plausible broken app that passes: an Express+SQLite app that writes inserts to SQLite but on boot 'compacts' positions by re-numbering each stage's cards by created_at/id (or keeps position/stage updates in an in-memory map flushed only on clean shutdown). Before restart, hro_moves/hro_bulk/hro_undo_activity pass (Mei reads the same order from the live server). hro_intake_restart passes too: J1's cards were only added, so insertion order equals stored order; the note, message, unread total and Activity lines are all inserts. After a real restart such an app silently loses every manual re-ordering (and, in the in-memory variant, every stage move and rejection reason), violating hireops_rules.md line 59-60, yet no criterion observes it. Conforming alternative that could fail unfairly: a fully durable app whose only fault is accepting places = 2.5 (or not keeping the typed source in the form after an email refusal) scores 0 on all 4.5 restart-durability weight because those intake legs share the binary.
suggested_fix: In hro_intake_restart, before restart_app, revise J1: move one card Applied->Screen, move another card up within Applied, reject a third with a suffixed reason, record each card's stage, within-stage order, reason and rejected-from stage, and re-read all of them after the restart (with the matching Activity lines); and consider splitting the restart/durability legs into their own criterion so intake-validation failures do not zero durability credit (rebalancing weights per the documented 1.0/1.5/2.0 leg scheme).
